feature: A screen can hug what it holds
summary: A screen set to a row or a column now has Width and Height rows with Hug or Fixed, the same as a group. With Hug picked the screen closes around what you drop into it and shrinks back when you take something out.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/a-screen-hugs-what-it-holds-walk.json

try.do: New Window, Blank canvas, then pick the Frame tool and drag out a screen.
In the Layout section press Stack, then Column.
Press Hug on Width and Hug on Height. The empty screen keeps its size.
Open the Library, Comps, and drag the Button tile onto the screen.
Drag the Card tile onto the screen as well.
Pick the Card in the Layers list, choose Edit > Delete, then press Command Z.
Pick the screen, press Fixed on Height and type 400 in H.

evaluate: When the first Button lands, is a screen snapping down to exactly the button's size what you expected from Hug?
Should a screen that starts hugging get some padding by default, so its edge does not sit right on the button?
Does an empty screen keeping its drawn size after Hug read as right, or as Hug doing nothing?
Is it clear that dragging a handle or typing a size turns that side back to Fixed?
rough: The mock draws one Frame size row (Hug, Narrow, Wide); the app shows Width and Height rows, each Hug or Fixed, as it already does for groups. Waiting on your answer in decision the-size-rows-in-the-layout-section-match-the-au-how-should-the-layout-section-le.
A screen made into a column while empty starts with 0 padding, so after Hug its edge sits flush on what it holds. Type a Padding to get room around the contents.
Screens get no Smallest or Largest size under Width and Height. Those stay a group's.
